en: The Ritual Manual of the King of Great Teachings on the Supreme Meaning of All Secrets,
Volume One.
This is extracted in brief from the extensive Yoga Tantra.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master and Dharma-transmitting Great Master Shi Hu, a purple-robed śramaṇa and subject, by Imperial Decree. I take refuge in all Buddhas.

The five bodies are produced by the Creator; One does not perceive a determinate body of sentient beings, Nor does one perceive a determinate mind; Contemplating and visualizing the Buddhas is likewise!

O Great Being, if you wish to prostrate to the Buddha, you should prostrate to your own authentic wisdom; for the Buddha’s wisdom and one's own wisdom originate from the same source, being non-dual within their secret nature.
If one realizes that all that arises is without self, that which arises is non-dual wisdom;
having attained liberation amidst the pleasant and the unpleasant, one prostrates to that which is signless and non-existent.
Dharmas have not arisen, nor do they arise now; what has arisen has already passed away and does not abide in the present.
Contemplate that the marks of all Buddhas are likewise so; one should prostrate to one’s own true wisdom.
Love and non-love have no inherent state; they stir and disturb according to the minds of sentient beings.
Within the faults of defiled seeds and afflictions, all corresponding phenomena are fully accomplished.
Sentient beings have suffering because they have bodies; this suffering arises from the mind as its cause.
If one thoroughly understands the mind, one is able to escape from all suffering.
All Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time are subsumed within the single Buddha Vairocana;
since all those Buddhas have perfected their realization of enlightenment, they manifest in the form of Buddhas to rescue beings from birth and death.
For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, The compassionate mind gives rise to skillful means;
Since the causal nature is thus in accord, The resultant nature emerges therefrom.
Because the fruit is real, one abides in equanimity; that cause is shown as the characteristic of seeking.
If within this there is a mind of real seeking, it immediately grows the seeds of saṃsāra.
Corresponding phenomena arise from correspondence; The phenomena one cherishes cannot be found.
That which is attained is but a single phenomenon persisting; It is precisely not free from the marks of conceptual discrimination.
With right mindfulness, contemplate the Buddha as being without objective referent; with right mindfulness, contemplate the Dharma in accordance with the Dharma;
the same applies to the two practices of self and others—this is what the Buddha, the Honored One among Two-Legged Beings, has always taught.
Having dwelt in accordance with reality within one's own specific characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa*), one visualizes entering into the images of all Buddhas;
through right mindfulness, one contemplates the Buddha and attains union, whereby clouds of Buddhas manifest from this.
Having established oneself as it truly is in one's own characteristic, one visualizes entering into the vajra-dharmatā;
through right mindfulness, one contemplates the dharma and attains union, giving rise to great clouds of Dharma that pervade everywhere.
"Characteristics" (lakṣaṇa) refers to the meaning of signs and marks; "destruction" is precisely the mind that destroys characteristics.
The four kinds are the gate of characteristic-signs; being able to destroy afflictions is the most supreme.
One's own self is identical to all sentient beings; one's own mind encompasses all phenomena.
By attaining realization within the selflessness of phenomena, all demons are thereby extinguished of their own accord.
Having realized one's own mind as it truly is, that realized mind cannot be apprehended;
having correctly understood one's own mind as it truly is, the minds of all māras are likewise so.
Correspondence is the nature of union; this nature cannot be found through seeking.
If one contemplates the Buddhas with such correspondence, then I am indeed identical to all Buddhas.
Born from the wisdom of samādhi, it is the equal self-nature of all Buddhas;
since the practice corresponding to the Buddha is not non-existent, one attains Buddhahood through the mind of correspondence.
If one perceives anything within the wondrous nature, that coarse and defiled nature cannot be eliminated;
if one regards nature and non-nature as distinct, the mind of contemplation is itself discrimination.
One cannot observe nature by means of nature; herein, even observation has nothing to be observed.
Both the observation of mental constructs and nature are non-existent; their differentiation arises from the movement and fluctuation of the mind.
It is neither the realm of sentient beings nor the realm of Buddhas; herein there is neither Buddha nor sentient being.
The self-mind of sentient beings is itself the Buddha-mind; through awakening, one realizes there is neither Buddha nor Buddha-wisdom.
If one perceives the nature of causes as they truly are, and likewise perceives the nature of effects as they truly are,
this is the gateway to the wisdom of samādhi— the practice of equality through non-dual correspondence.
The causal nature of all phenomena cannot be apprehended, and the resultant nature of all phenomena is likewise so;
because they are observed through true wisdom, their nature is fundamentally real—this is precisely the practice of corresponding equality.
Phenomena are fundamentally without cause, yet one contemplates causes; phenomena are fundamentally without fruit, yet one contemplates fruits.
If one contemplates anything within cause and fruit, this is precisely the arising of attachment from one's own mind.
When contemplating causes, one should contemplate the cause of true wisdom; when contemplating effects, one should contemplate the secret effect.
Within the non-dual union of the secret, one should thus observe for oneself.
If one can thoroughly understand true reality, one understands the secret within secrets;
having thoroughly understood this profound secret, one accomplishes the supreme practice of union.
If one is equanimous toward objects of attachment, that is the very nature of objects of non-attachment;
though the Tathāgata contemplates all the various marks of objects of attachment and non-attachment, he perceives nothing therein.
When the practitioner is in union, union arises; it is not non-manifest, nor is it without measure.
When one’s own wisdom enters the gate of purity, all Buddhas and Tathāgatas are likewise pure.
From this, the body, speech, and mind arise; The secret practice of non-dual union;
The first four measures of the gateways of clear realization, Which are the four mudrā methods of union itself.
The karma-mudrā is the seal of the body’s secret;
the dharma-mudrā is called the seal of speech’s secret;
the mahāmudrā is the gateway of the mind’s seal, while the samaya-mudrā seals all.
Visualizing all mudrās as sealing all phenomena, one is then in union with the three aspects of the Lord of Secrets;
through realizing the suchness of intrinsic nature, the wisdom of samādhi is skillfully applied.
Through the clear manifestation of the excellence of body, speech, and mind, various phenomena arise as the signs of the teachings;
yet, because they do not depart from the three doors of secret mantra, they are established by means of the skillful activity of Vajra.
The true wisdom of the Tathāgatas of the five families is itself the secret, unsurpassed wisdom;
if one accords with the four secret seals, one can achieve the siddhi of the language of yoga.
The four great elements—earth, water, fire, and wind—are precisely the four secret mudrās that have been taught;
when these four seals are equalized and brought into union, the four vidyā-rājñīs are all assembled together.
Buddhalocanā Bodhisattvī is the earth element;
Māmakī is the water element; Pāṇḍaravāsinī Bodhisattvī is the fire element.
The Bodhisattva Tārā is the element of wind;
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, in the eastern direction is the element of earth;
Varuṇa, Lord of the Devas, in the western direction is the element of water.
The Fire Deity of the south is the fire element;
the Wind Deity of the north is the wind element.
One should know that Śakra is yellow; for the *puṣṭi* (augmenting) rite, the mandala shape is square.
The altar of Varuṇa is white and circular; for the rite of pacification, one should act according to the instructions.
The altar of Agni is red and triangular; for the rite of subjugation through affection, one should follow the original ritual.
The altar of Vāyu is black and bow-shaped; with a wrathful mind, one performs the rite of subduing.
Arising from the four great elements, the four types of activities follow in their respective order;
by turning this wheel of the four activities, the supreme siddhi is fully perfected.
For pacifying, one should rely on the method of Buddhalocanā;
for increasing, the method of Padmavajrā;
for magnetizing, the method of Vairocana.
Regarding the method for subduing with Vajra-anger:
at the first watch of the night, one should perform the rite of pacification (*śāntika*);
at dawn, one should perform that rite of augmentation (*puṣṭika*).
At midday, one should perform the rite of subjugation;
at midnight, the rite of attraction.
For the pacification rite, the image of the noble deity should be white.
For the purpose of increasing prosperity, the image of a noble being is yellow;
for the purpose of winning affection, the image of a noble being is red;
for the purpose of subjugation, the image of a noble being is black.
Know that when the wisdom of samādhi arises, the activities of the supreme siddhis are accomplished;
by visualizing all Buddhas as fundamentally pure, all Buddha-activities are fully realized.
Vairocana Buddha in the center!
Tathāgatas of the Vajradhātu in the four directions!
Visualizing the true bodies of the lords of the five families, all that is undertaken shall be accomplished.
Within the mind, one should further visualize the Great Wisdom Consort!
The practitioner who maintains the method of union is able to give birth to the bodies of all Buddhas; she is the Mother of the Vajradhātu!
The three poisons of the world—greed, hatred, and delusion—are themselves the Tathāgata Vajradhātu!
Through the Buddha’s gate of secret purity, one realizes that those three poisons become non-poisonous;
thus, by means of greed, hatred, and delusion, one attains mastery within the three realms.
The Great Beings, the Buddhas, shatter the poisonous mind; To contemplate it as such is the wisdom of all Buddhas.
If one realizes that the Buddhas are free from a mind of greed, Then the bodhicitta arises from the very nature of greed;
Furthermore, one can give rise to the practices of Samantabhadra— The greedy mind is itself the Buddha Tathāgata!
If one understands that the Buddhas tame the mind, Subtle wisdom emerges from the very nature of anger;
Furthermore, it can give birth to all-encompassing knowledge— The angry mind is itself the Buddha-Tathāgata!
If one can awaken to and realize this within one's own mind, that luminosity emerges from the very nature of delusion;
furthermore, it can give birth to all Buddhas—this deluded mind is itself the Buddha-Tathāgata!
If one realizes that all Buddhas are without a self-mind, All kinsmen and friends emerge from the view of self;
Furthermore, one can give birth to all Buddhas— The mind of loving-kindness is itself the Buddha-Tathāgata!
The universal observation and illumination of all Buddhas is love; The Dharma-discourse of all Buddhas is compassion;
All-fearlessness is the great gift— This is called the Dharma of the Buddhas’ Reverent Love.
The Stage of Joy is associated with generosity;
the Stainless Stage is the perfection of ethical discipline;
the Radiant Stage is the firmness of patience.
The Ground of Effulgent Wisdom through diligent exertion and striving;
the Ground of Manifestation through meditative concentration free from views;
and the Ground Difficult to Conquer through the realization of sublime wisdom.
The Ground of Far-Reaching Conduct, which possesses great skillful means;
the Ground of Immovability, in which supreme power is perfected;
and the Ground of Excellent Intelligence, in which vows are further expanded.
Through wisdom, one accomplishes the Dharma-Cloud Stage;
the wondrous wisdom-body of the Buddha-Tathāgata alone is called the fulfillment of the eleventh stage.
The ten sages cultivate the ten pāramitās, and the various practices of the ten powers reach their perfection.
Having thus transcended the ten stages, one then attains the dharmas corresponding to Buddhahood.
Drinking the water of the vajra, one achieves perfect enlightenment; through the nectar-flavor of the Dharma, one enters into union.
Becoming equal to all infinite Buddhas, one remains far removed from all grasping and abandoning.
The dharmas corresponding to primordial purity, and likewise the purification through drinking the vajra-water;
the nectar-flavor of the Dharma satisfies the mind, and so too it is for the vajra disciples.
Primordial purity is itself bodhi, and it is through this that the bodhicitta is subsequently attained;
if one abides in the sovereign bodhicitta, one should know that such a bodhisattva is indeed a Tathāgata.
One attains the state of liberation through correct reasoning, and the bodhicitta is unsurpassed;
if one abides in the mind of Vajrasattva, the corresponding dharmas will be accomplished in this very life.
The gate of samādhi of the three secrets of karma, Attaining the eye of samādhi to constantly observe and illuminate;
The realms and destinies of sentient beings are vast and boundless, Yet that mother of samādhi sustains them inexhaustibly.
Well-established in the body of the three vajras, one seals all things with the samaya-mudrā;
through the gateway of the dharma-mudrā of the samādhi of the three secrets, one never tires of the speech-vajra.
In all those worlds, extending even as far as the Yojana;
if one accords with the secret of the Great Seal Mind, the Vajra Mind will never grow weary or depart.
All paths beloved within the three realms, explained extensively even unto the Yojanas;
having fully known all beloved gateways, one experiences them all as they correspond without attachment.
Born from Vajrasattva, these are all the wondrous *yogīśvara* mudrās;
if one acts in accordance with their application, one attains sovereign mastery over all mudrās.
The practice of the supreme secret union gives rise to the gateway of samādhi-wisdom;
if the view of self does not arise therein, the syllable HŪṂ is not employed as an awakening call.
One need not rely on bodily action to perform deeds, such as arranging altars, binding mudrās, or constructing stūpas and images;
one need not rely on vocal action to maintain mantras and vidyās, and should likewise abandon the recitation of dharmas;
one should have no moving thoughts regarding mental action, treating the slight and the revered without distinction.
When these three karmas are brought into accord, this is the essential means for seeking the Buddha’s bodhi.
Regarding the four dharmas of killing, stealing, lust, and falsehood, do not give rise to a mind of protection toward them;
if the conceptualization of obstruction and prevention arises, know that it is itself defiled, yet eternally pure.
Performing the homa rite within meditative concentration, and all other activities without divergent thoughts;
when body, speech, and mind are fundamentally in accord with the secret [mantra], this is the supreme and vast practice.
If you wish to accomplish all vidyā-mantras, And desire to be in union with them in all places,
You should focus your mind with single-minded concentration And visualize the nature of all Buddha-dharmas.
All the eighteen unique qualities (āveṇika-dharmas) are what are called the Buddha-dharmas;
by constantly giving rise to the mind of contemplative visualization within them, the Bodhi of all Buddhas is attained.

The four dhyānas, the four samādhis, and the samādhi of cessation—having attained all such concentrations, one remains forever free from the notion of existence; only then is the Buddha’s bodhi fully accomplished.
Among all the dharma-gates of the bodhisattvas, those thirty-seven factors of enlightenment—
if one contemplates them with purity therein— will be able to bring benefit to the world.
All transformative minds in the world, when visualized as reality and remain unmoving, arise from emptiness; this is what is called vajra-wisdom.
Furthermore, from the selflessness of phenomena arises the non-dual, ultimate, supreme wisdom;
this supreme wisdom is itself the dharmatā, which is precisely what is called the Great Dharmadhātu.
One should know that the self-nature of the dharmadhātu is the mind accomplished through vajra-wisdom;
born from the diamond-like samādhi (vajropama-samādhi), this is precisely what is called the Vajradhātu.
Initially conjoined with subtle and wondrous wisdom, this conjoined mind is utterly vast;
from which the all-knowing wisdom of all Tathāgatas arises—this is indeed Vairocana Buddha!
The supreme gateway for practitioners of the path, Whose compassionate conduct is most vast;
With an untainted, true, and immovable mind— This is what is called the Buddha Akṣobhya!
Skillfully performing deeds that gather and sustain sentient beings, With practices of compassion that are utterly vast;
Possessing a harmonious mind that benefits all beings— This is precisely what is named the Buddha Ratnasambhava!
The supreme Mahāyāna, free from defilement, Is the vast and expansive practice associated with joy;
With a mind of pure, radiant, and translucent clarity— This is what is called Amitāyus!
Awakened to all classes of sentient beings, Skillfully relinquishing with a most vast mind;
With the non-empty, unsurpassed, wondrously applied mind— This is the Buddha Amoghasiddhi!
The dharma of the samādhi of unsurpassed bodhi—this dharma is named Vajra Wisdom;
born from this Vajra Wisdom is none other than the Bodhisattva Vajrasattva!
Excellent with the supreme vajra hook, he is universally able to summon all Buddhas;
the king among all Vajra families—this is the Bodhisattva Vajrarāja!
Skilled in the supreme rite of loving-kindness, he is able to inspire love in all Buddhas;
with a great heart, he does not abandon even Māra—this is the Bodhisattva Vajrarāga!
All Buddhas are filled with joy, Praising: "Excellent! Well done!
Having attained the joy of all those Buddhas, This is indeed the Bodhisattva Vajrasādhu!
The great, precious jewel, non-empty and unimpeded, From which such jewels as these arise, equaling space;
Universally bestowed upon all Buddhas and the assembly of sages— This is the Bodhisattva Vajraratna!
Wisdom is pure because it is free from ignorance; likewise, all conditioned phenomena are without attachment.
This radiant light of liberation, this great illumination—this is the Bodhisattva Vajraprabha!
Realizing the path of liberation as it truly is, he attains the wisdom perfected by all marks;
taking the banner of the True Dharma as his great banner—this is the Bodhisattva Vajraketu!
The Bodhisattva’s heart rejoices and emits a great sigh; this is the Great Corresponding Vajra-Laughter.
It causes all Buddhas to be universally delighted; this is the Bodhisattva Vajrahāsa!
The nature of all phenomena is the purity of the Tathāgata; One is able to realize and awaken to all Buddha-dharmas;
Being able to enter into great resonance with all Buddhas— This is the Bodhisattva Vajradharma!
The wondrous wisdom of the Mahāyāna is exceedingly sharp, Able to sever all seeds of affliction;
It likewise shatters the cognitive obscurations— This is the Bodhisattva Vajratīkṣṇa!
The Great Being is the subtle cause of the Mahāyāna; He follows and accords with the Tathāgata’s wheel of speech.
Because of the Buddha’s words, he turns the Wheel of Dharma; This is the Bodhisattva Vajrahetu!
Adorned with wisdom, his speech is pure, Transcending all sounds of conceptual discrimination;
His wondrous voice resounds in harmony with the Dharma— This is the Bodhisattva Vajrabhāṣa!
Adorned with wisdom and purified through karma, He manifests every gateway of transformative signs as they arise;
Able to accomplish all supreme deeds— This is the Bodhisattva Vajrakarma!
The method of practice corresponding to the contemplation of the Buddha with right mindfulness, acting in accordance with the conduct of the bodhicitta;
with a right mind remaining far removed from other vehicles—this is the Bodhisattva Vajrapāla!
Those with sharp fangs who devour those of sinful karma— The principle of extinguishing all afflictions is likewise so;
Because afflictions are exhausted, wondrous function is accomplished: This is the Bodhisattva Vajradaṃṣṭra!
The three secrets of vajra body, speech, and mind can exhaust all limits of bondage;
when wisdom abides within the true nature of suchness, this is the Bodhisattva Vajramuṣṭi!
The Ritual Manual of the King of Great Teachings, the Supreme Meaning of All Secrets, Volume One;
The Ritual Manual of the King of Great Teachings, the Supreme Meaning of All Secrets,
Volume Two.

Translated by the Tripitaka Master and Dharma-transmitting Grand Master Shi Hu, a subject who received the purple robe, by imperial decree: The Dharma of the *Dānapāramitā* (Perfection of Giving) Is the Great Vajra Play (*Vajralalita*).
Sporting with sovereign mastery and ever-pure, This is the Bodhisattva Vajralalita!
The dharma of the perfection of ethical discipline is the wondrous jewel garland of vajra;
adorning body and mind, it is entirely pure—this is the Bodhisattva Vajramālā!
The Dharma of the perfection of patience is the sublime vajra song;
the well-collected udāna of the true Dharma—this is the Bodhisattva Vajragīta!
The dharma of the perfection of diligence is the sublime vajra dance;
before long one shall attain the bodhi of a Buddha—this is the Vajranṛtya Bodhisattva!
The Dharma of the Great Wisdom Perfection is itself the supreme incense of the vajra;
pervasive in all places and vast without limit—this is the Vajragandhā Bodhisattva!
The dharma of the perfection of meditative concentration is the exquisite vajra-flower;
like a lotus born from the mud yet unstained by it, this is the Bodhisattva Vajrapuṣpa!
The dharma of the perfection of supreme vows is the vast vajra lamp;
illuminating everywhere throughout all places, this is the Bodhisattva Vajrapradīpa!
The dharma of the perfection of skillful means is the sublime vajra unguent;
it completely purifies all foul odors—this is the Honored One of Vajra Unguent!
The great skillful means of all Tathāgatas distinguish four kinds of secret signs;
the great skillful means of all *karmas*—this is the Bodhisattva Vajrāṅkuśa!
The practice of the bodhisattva path through union is the supreme vajra;
that firm and sublime nature is the Bodhisattva Vajrasaṃhara.
All phenomena are fundamentally unarisen, Primordially pure and equal to space;
This true essence of the Dharma-speech Is the Bodhisattva Vajraghaṇṭā!
Contemplating that all is the unsurpassed bodhicitta, Which originates from the supreme buddha-nature;
The establishment of the names of the pāramitās— This is the Vajrasattva Honored One!
The Great Wisdom Perfection is pure, From which the four means of attraction arise;
These four means of attraction bring boundless benefit— This is the Bodhisattva Ratnavajra!
The purity of the true *pāramitās* gives rise to the Great *Pāramitā*;
this secret gateway of the wisdom of equality is the Bodhisattva Dharmavajra!
The purity of the Vajra-pāramitā is itself the sovereign of the four pāramitās;
all ritual actions are entirely in accord with it—this is the Honored One, Karma-vajra!
The perfection of great wisdom is pure; it is the nature of the vajra perfection.
Universally corresponding with all secrets, from this the twelve marks are born.
One should know that from Vajrapāṇi arise all the secret mudrās of samādhi;
these two firm vajra-fists are called the karma-mudrā.
Born from the wisdom of the equality of non-self, Free from marks, unimpeded, and free from the view of self;
All defiled attachments are completely purified— This is the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi!
This explains the causal conditions for vajra passion; it is itself the unsurpassed wisdom of the vajra.
The dharma of passion is further the pure lotus; the flower is the wondrous dharma-wisdom of the vajra.
If one realizes that one’s own seed arises from its own characteristic, then all Buddhas are subsumed within this;
if the two kinds of emanations are brought into correspondence, this is the true offering of Vajrasattva.
Great wisdom thoroughly understands its own seeds; the two dharmas of compassion and love are then united.
Abiding in meditative equipoise through the correspondence of these two bases, one destroys duality by means of non-dual dharma.
Abiding in the maṇḍala of equality, from this emerges the great method of correspondence;
jesting, speech, dancing, and singing—all these are the skillful means of the Buddha’s words.
Within the union of the two practices of self and other, one manifests deeds that benefit all sentient beings;
its nature is luminous and primordially pure—this is the maṇḍala of the moon of mind.
Greed is fundamentally pure like a lotus flower; all enemies of the afflictions are utterly severed.
That which is expressed by the initial words is this very Mahācakra Maṇḍala.
The self-nature is luminously pure from the beginning, And the bodhicitta is unsurpassed;
Accomplishing the welfare of all sentient beings— This is the Maṇḍala of the Wondrous Moon.
Adorned with the purity of wisdom, it arises from that vajra-like samādhi;
the light of liberation and the light of equanimity—this is the maṇḍala of the sun disc.
When the equality of the five Buddhas is realized, the functions of the five wisdoms are harmoniously integrated;
with the five eyes purified for clear observation, this is the maṇḍala of the five Buddhas.
The vajra can shatter all things; holding the hook symbolizes the practice of union.
That supreme and wondrous vajra-arrow—excellent! brings about the joy of virtuous deeds.
Fully endowed with all adornments such as jewels;
the sun’s light arises, radiating great brilliance;
he establishes the supreme and wondrous banner of vajra.
This is the manifestation of the Vajra Laughter!
The nature of all things, the Vajra of Skillful Action, is by its very nature an indestructible practice of union;
manifesting the form of bared fangs, one attains union, and all mudrās are thereby accomplished.
The four kinds of vidyā-mudrās are universally in union; In play, whether walking or staying, they are without obstruction.
With the fine, new thread spun by Nārī, One skillfully measures the boundaries according to their proportions.
Abiding in the visualization of body, speech, and mind, one should establish the boundary-path with the wisdom-thread;
according to the ritual, one arrays the maṇḍala with four sides, four gates, and four pavilions.
Divide the corners of the altar into four equal lines, marked with the signs of *nīrgha* and *vitasti*;
adorn them with half- and full-necklaces, precious fly-whisks, and garlands of the seven precious gems.
Within the maṇḍala, arrange exquisite lotus flowers; the heart-maṇḍala is the most supreme.
The pavilion is itself true wisdom, with its peak of wisdom rising high and manifest.
Contemplating the appearance of that mandala’s exterior four sides, all sentient beings emerge from them;
the four types of mind—loving-kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity—are represented by these four lines.
If the four lines spoken of are equal, one is then in accord with right mindfulness regarding phenomena;
if one is not liberated from all views, one attains liberation through the line of wisdom.
The lotuses adorning the center of the maṇḍala represent the supreme practice of pure ethical discipline;
the five boundary walls at the center of the four directions represent the five excellent faculties, such as faith;
and the description of the maṇḍala gates throughout represents the dharma-gates of the eight liberations.
The four multi-storied pavilions at the four gates represent the four right efforts;
the four *vitarkas* within the maṇḍala represent the four foundations of mindfulness;
and those four *nirhāras* represent the four bases of psychic power.
The exquisite adornment of garlands of the seven precious gems represents the seven factors of enlightenment;
the four gates and eight pillars should be known as representing the eightfold noble path.
By means of the wisdom of that samādhi, one is able to achieve liberation from the two obscurations;
the exquisite jewel-whisks within the maṇḍala represent the wisdom of the supreme path.
The complete set of necklaces within the maṇḍala symbolizes the total severance of all afflictions;
since the substance of the necklaces is supreme wisdom, all afflictions can be eliminated and severed.
That which possesses half a necklace represents the halving of all afflictions;
because the two practices of self and other are in accord, the afflictions of the coverings and entanglements are severed by half.
Selflessness is equal to space, and non-attachment is the most supreme wondrous wisdom;
because the mind of attachment is pure, there is also no duality—this is what is called the Ornament of Wisdom.
If one attains bodhi through non-attachment, then bodhi would differ from the mind of attachment;
since the essence of the bodhicitta is without distinction, therefore attachment and non-attachment are not two.
The world consists of two types: those with desire and those without desire; one should skillfully contemplate them through expedient means.
The methods for accomplishing mudrās arise from desire, and all other [accomplishments] are likewise achieved.
If one dwells in the world with a disciplined mind, Then one gives rise to corresponding conduct of equanimity;
When the undisciplined mind is purified, This very craving is itself an offering.
All the extensively explained characteristics of conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*) are merely the characteristics of the sphere of conceptual discrimination;
if one abides in the gateway of the seals of body, speech, and mind, that which is sealed is none other than true wisdom.
If one contemplates this mudrā in accordance with it, one will always possess mastery among all mudrās;
and if one thoroughly understands this method of mudrā, one will accomplish the visualization of all mudrās.
When the various objective signs are in harmony, one knows them and acts with equanimity in accordance with them;
if all these signs are thus brought into accord, all siddhis will be perfectly fulfilled.
The insignia within all secrets: the right hand symbolizes the gate of wisdom;
the left represents the gate of compassion, and the same applies to their meanings—one should constantly perform visualization according to what they signify.
When the two hands are joined in the mudrā, it symbolizes the two kinds of samādhi;
the markings on the soles of the two feet symbolize the practice of benefiting both oneself and others.
When the five fingers are equal and in union, they symbolize the adornment of the five maṇḍalas;
the five Buddhas manifest as perfectly awakened ones, each representing its respective order.
The middle finger represents the arising of space;
the index finger symbolizes the altar of the Earth Deity;
and the ring and little fingers [represent the remaining elements].
When visualizing the mandalas of the water, fire, wind,
and sky elements in their respective order at the navel wheel, they represent the Vajradhātvīśvarī;
if one further performs visualization at the heart, they represent the Lord Sattvavajra.
The space between the eyebrows represents Ratnavajra;
the neck represents Dharmavajra;
and the crown of the head represents Karmavajra.
Visualize clearly according to what is symbolized:
the five Buddhas manifest as perfectly awakened ones; the five wisdoms are fully perfected and accomplished.
When the five types of color-forms correspond, the five maṇḍalas appear.
If there is something heard in the preceding sound, it indicates the preceding name and phrase;
if there is something heard in the subsequent sound, it indicates the subsequent meaning.
Furthermore, that which is heard in the preceding sound signifies the meaning of the cause;
that which is heard in the subsequent sound signifies the meaning of the effect.
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess no dualistic dharmas; within this, cause and effect cannot be apprehended.
Within the dharma-gate of the fundamental absence of intrinsic nature, for this reason all dharmas are eternally abiding.

To awaken to one's own mind is itself to be a Buddha; when the awakening mind and the object of awakening are both forgotten, within the realm of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas, the bodhicitta is without distinction.
The luminous nature of all sentient beings is equal in appearance across all places;
since the nature of sentient beings is fundamentally pure, bodhi is established thereby.
With the mind unmoved, well-secured by locks, the nature of firmness is spontaneously accomplished;
visualizing the mind in meditative equipoise within the topknot, one dons armor to protect the body, ever courageous and strong.
All Buddhas perfectly realize that vajra speech is the Tathāgata;
The two places and the gate of samāpatti are no different from Vairocana Buddha.
Within the Dharma, twelve years represent the Buddha Tathāgata;
sixteen years signify the sixteen deities, such as Vajrapāṇi and the others.
The twenty-year-olds are the various Nairṛtis; they are the secret twenty deities!
Performing twenty kinds of offerings, those twenty assemblies should be arranged in their respective order.
That which arises from one's own family is what is called "one's own vidyā-mantra";
that which arises from another family is what is called "another's vidyā-mantra."
Truly understanding all that is to be done, the mind-maṇḍala is supreme;
in performing all offerings, one must be single-minded and diligent, making offerings through body, speech, and mind.
From the union of the vajra and lotus, they arise in equal measure from both places;
visualizing one's own seed-syllable as the form of the Buddha is the true offering of Vajrasattva.
Half- and full-necklaces, jeweled whisks, and so forth—these various ornaments are as described previously;
the dimensions of the maṇḍala herein should be twelve or sixteen cubits.
Next, it gradually increases by twenty cubits until it completely encompasses the maṇḍala;
when twenty-five cubits are required, one should then construct it at the measure of twenty-five cubits.
Within the sections of the maṇḍala gates, distribute them into nine parts according to the ritual manual;
distribute the nīrgha as appropriate, having carefully considered the maṇḍala gates.
Construct the inner maṇḍala equally; the maṇḍala is half a nyūha.
Thus, without departing from the nine divisions, properly arrange it at the corners of the maṇḍala.
In the four directions of the maṇḍala, one should appropriately arrange the four vaitis;
if the five colors are blended and harmonized, they shall serve as the adornment for the five maṇḍalas.
The five eyes observe and purify all evils; the five colors are themselves the five Tathāgatas!
Through the correspondence with the dharma of the equality of the five Buddhas, the ground is adorned with the marks of the five colors.
Within the five maṇḍalas, one should visualize the five Buddhas installed according to their respective directions;
the five kinds of merit are all perfectly complete, and the five colors are the five samādhis.
The ground at the center of the maṇḍala is pure, with the wondrous color of the light of the moon-love maṇi;
the ground in the eastern direction is a great blue color;
the southern direction is yellow, according to the ritual manual.
In the west, it is red as appropriate;
in the north, the color of maṇiṣṭha.
In all locations, the *vaidūrya* mark is used, except that it should not be applied to the central path of the gate.
Within the maṇḍala is Vairocana Buddha!
Visualize him manifesting the appearance of crystal moonlight;
he is the unified embodiment of all Buddhas, and he is none other than the Tathāgata Abhayacakṣus.
Visualize Akṣobhya Buddha in the eastern direction!
He manifests with the appearance of a brilliant blue light;
all vajras are unified within him—this is the Tathāgata Vajralocana!
Visualize Ratnasambhava Buddha in the south!
He manifests the golden light of Jambudvīpa;
all Buddhas universally gather and benefit sentient beings—this is indeed the Tathāgata Prabhālocana!
Visualize Amitāyus in the western direction!
A great light of lotus color appears;
born from the wisdom of phenomena, it is the Great Fearlessness—this is the Tathāgata Padmanetra!
In the north is Buddha Amoghasiddhi!
He manifests the appearance of light rays in the color of makara;
universally gathering all sentient beings so they are likewise born [in that state], he is the Tathāgata Maitreya-locana!
Furthermore, one should visualize within the maṇḍala the supreme, wondrous, and unsurpassed wisdom of all Buddhas;
from the realm of space arises the most sublime and excellent Moon Maṇḍala.
Having visualized the images of all the Buddhas within, next visualize the venerable Bodhisattva Locanā!
Her pure eyes are long and wide, her face is dignified and beautiful;
she possesses the wondrous color of the moon-love maṇi jewel, and all the marks and parts of her body are perfectly complete—she is the most supreme among all vidyārājñīs.
Visualize holding a great wheel in hand, causing all throughout the three realms to be universally inspired with reverence and love;
next, visualize the wisdom that accomplishes activities— this wisdom is equal to the realm of space,
appearing within the space-vajra as the most supreme and wondrous moon-maṇḍala.
Having visualized the images of all Buddhas within, one next visualizes the noble deity Māmakī:
with pure eyes, long and wide, and a face of serene majesty;
the color of a blue utpala lotus, with all physical marks and limbs perfectly complete; the supreme venerable one, a magical manifestation of space.
Holding a blue utpala lotus in hand, he causes all within the three realms to take refuge.
Next, one should contemplate the pure wisdom of bodhi; this wisdom is equal to the realm of empty space, appearing from within the vajra of emptiness as the most supreme and wondrous moon maṇḍala.
Having visualized the images of the Buddhas within, next visualize the venerable Bodhisattva Śvetāmbara!
With pure eyes, long and wide, and a face of dignified beauty; with the wondrous color of the light of a lotus-maṇi;
all the marks and limbs of his body perfectly complete; he is the Honored One of Secret Vajra Dharma Wisdom.
Holding a red utpala lotus in hand, one attains the constant contemplative vision of all Buddhas.
Next, one should visualize the wisdom of vajra-meditative concentration;
this wisdom is equal to the realm of empty space, and from this very emptiness arises the most supreme and wondrous moon maṇḍala.
Having visualized the images of all the Buddhas within, next visualize the Venerable Tārābodhi!
With pure eyes, long and wide, and a face of serene majesty, her supreme color is the wondrous luster of refined gold;
all the marks and limbs of her body are perfectly complete—she is the Consort, the Sovereign Goddess of Playful Sport.
Holding a yellow utpala lotus in hand, all sentient beings take refuge [in her].
Thus are the heart-mantras of those four Bodhisattvas.
The great mantra of the Bodhisattva Buddhalocanā is as follows:
Oṃ ruru saphuru jvala tiṣṭha siddhalocane sarvārthasādhani svāhā. The Great Mantra of the Bodhisattva Māmakī is:
Oṃ śaṅkari śāntikari ghuṭa ghuṭa ghuṭini gata gata gati svāhā. The Great Mantra of the Bodhisattva Pāṇḍaravāsini is:
Oṃ kaci vikaci nikaci kacitkaci karuṇavīrye svāhā. The Great Mantra of the Bodhisattva Tārā is as follows: Oṃ tāre tuttāre ture svāhā.

These four kinds of great mantras of the four bodhisattvas encompass the secret activities of body, speech, and mind. Among all forms of worship, these are the true worship. The three secrets of the Vajra universally protect all; they are constantly produced in all places, and there is nothing among all that is done which is not accomplished.

The nature of these dharmas associated with yoga is intrinsically pure; those practitioners who cultivate yoga should understand them as they truly are and act accordingly, whereby they will attain genuine accomplishment.

Why is this? Because these corresponding practices are born from secret wisdom; they are precisely the wisdom of the samādhi of skillful means (upāya) within the Prajñāpāramitā. By means of this, all activities can be accomplished, and all saṃsāra is rendered completely pure.
Just as the self-nature of the supreme jewel is constantly illuminated by its own light, so too is the purity of saṃsāra.

Furthermore, if a practitioner who is in union is able to skillfully cultivate this dharma-gate of union, they are one who possesses great love and delight within the Vajradhātu; they will further perfect the great wisdom of liberation and achieve the four secret dharmas. As the Buddhas have taught, such a person is called a "Great Wise One"!
